title: Unified release pipeline for SDKs with language-specific publishlets and signed provenance
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Our SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) are published via ad-hoc CI jobs across several repos. Releases often diverge in tagging, packaging options, and provenance metadata. We lack a single reproducible pipeline that: 1) performs language-specific packaging (wheel/sdist, npm pack, go module proxy upload), 2) produces signed artifacts and an attestation/provenance bundle, 3) runs controlled canary promotions to internal registries and then promotes to public registries, and 4) supports reproducible builds for audit/compliance.

Goal: Build a unified release pipeline that runs from a single release workflow template, spawns small language-specific publishlets (packagers/publishers) for each SDK repo, emits provenance metadata (in-toto/COSIGN attestation JSON), signs artifacts with an ephemeral KMS-backed key, and supports safe promotion with automated rollback. The pipeline should be runnable in both GitHub Actions and Buildkite variants and include example client verification steps and docs.

Scope:
- Implement CI workflow templates and per-language publishlets (python, ts, go).
- Produce reproducible build outputs (deterministic timestamps, pinned dependencies where applicable).
- Integrate cosign/in-toto for attestation signing, with optional KMS-backed signing in infra.
- Canary publish to internal registries (test PyPI, npm internal, private Go proxy), automated smoke tests against example apps.
- Promotion automation to public registries including npm dist-tag handling and PyPI upload with 2FA requirements.

Out of scope: Private on-prem artifact transfer (will require infra work tracked separately), build-system refactors beyond packaging, and legacy single-repo release scripts (we will deprecate them after rollout).
acceptance_criteria: A single templated release workflow exists that can be parameterized per SDK repo
Python: wheels and sdist produced reproducibly and uploaded to internal index; artifacts signed and attestation generated
TypeScript: package tarball produced with fixed lockfile, smoke test against example service; npm publish to internal registry then canary promotion to 'next' dist-tag
Go: module zip + go.mod verification uploaded to internal proxy and optionally published to public proxy with metadata attestations
Artifacts and attestations are signed using cosign with KMS-backed ephemeral key; verification documented and automated in CI smoke step
Canary promotion runbook and automatic rollback on post-release health failures
Docs: step-by-step publish guide, CLI commands for verifying provenance locally, and changelog generation examples
At least two SDK repos (one Python, one TS) adopt the pipeline and complete a full canary -> public promotion in staging
Security review completed for signing approach and key handling
Monitoring/alerting dashboard for publish failures and artifact verification coverage
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ravi Patel: Kickoff spike completed. Evaluated cosign vs GPG for artifact signing; cosign + KMS looks simpler for ephemeral keys and integrates with OCI-style attestations. Spikes: reproducible Python wheels using setuptools reproducible-builds flags; npm pack with fixed time using node-tar tweaks.

2026-03-11 - Morgan Chen: POC CI templates created in private repo. Python publishlet builds wheel+sdist, uses python-reproducible-builds patch. Found flaky test on Windows for sdist metadata -> added a containerized build to standardize timestamps.

2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor (Security): Reviewed signing plan. Security notes: require KMS key rotation policy, restrict GitHub Actions to use short-lived credentials only. Requested an explicit threat model document and audit plan for key compromise.

2026-03-13 - Morgan Chen: Discovered npm dist-tag promotion bug when promoting 'latest' directly caused a small spike in consumers pulling prerelease. Implemented 'next' dist-tag staging plus manual approval gate. Added smoke-test harness for example integration testing post-publish.

2026-03-14 - Ravi Patel: CI matrix expanded to include Buildkite variant for internal infra teams. Created PRs and addendum docs. Plan: run two pilot releases next week (python-sdk -> test PyPI -> public; ts-sdk -> internal npm -> next -> public).
2026-03-14 - Design review note: include concise verification UX in Console so customers can see artifact signatures and release provenance on SDK package pages. Filed follow-up PM task.
